data.name: Khai Jiao Moo Sap with Rice
data.description: A golden Thai omelet puffs around tender minced pork, with crisp, lacy edges and savory fish sauce throughout. Fragrant jasmine rice catches the rich juices beneath its airy center.

refrigerator.notes: Transfer leftovers to shallow containers and refrigerate promptly, ideally within 1 hour for the rice. Keep at 4°C (40°F) or below and eat within 24 hours.

freezer.notes: Cool promptly and freeze the rice and omelet in separate airtight containers. The omelet loses some crispness after freezing. Thaw in the refrigerator.

storage.reheating: Reheat the rice covered in a microwave and the omelet in a skillet until both reach 74°C (165°F) throughout. Reheat only once.

equipment.name: Small saucepan with a tight-fitting lid
Thermometer suitable for frying oil and food
Microwave with a microwave-safe covered dish

items.name: jasmine rice
items.notes: Use white jasmine rice; the cooking time does not apply to brown rice.

items.name: water
items.notes: Cooking water for the rice; keep the saucepan tightly covered during simmering.

items.name: eggs
items.notes: Approximately 2 large eggs; weigh the contents without shells.

items.name: ground pork
items.notes: Use boneless pork mince, preferably about 15–20% fat.

items.name: fish sauce
items.notes: Use fish sauce made from fish and salt, with or without sugar.

items.name: canola oil
items.notes: Use as a shallow frying bath in the small pan. Lift the cooked omelet out of the oil; leave the remaining oil in the pan to cool before disposal.

instructions.text: Bring the jasmine rice and 120 g water to a gentle boil in the small saucepan over medium-high heat, about 3 minutes.
Simmer the rice over the lowest heat with the lid tightly closed for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Keep the lid closed throughout cooking.

doneness_cues.visual: No standing water remains when the lid is opened after resting.

instructions.text: Rest the covered rice off the heat for 5 minutes. Prepare the omelet mixture and heat its oil during this rest.

doneness_cues.tactile: The rice grains are tender throughout.

instructions.text: Mix the pork, fish sauce and white pepper in the mixing bowl with a fork, separating the mince into small, loose pieces. Keep raw pork and its utensils away from the cooked rice and serving plate; wash your hands and clean contaminated surfaces after handling it.

doneness_cues.visual: The pork is evenly seasoned with no large clumps.

instructions.text: Beat the eggs into the pork mixture with the whisk for about 45 seconds, until frothy and evenly combined.

doneness_cues.visual: Small bubbles cover the surface, and the pork is dispersed through the eggs.

instructions.text: Heat the canola oil in the high-sided frying pan over medium-high heat to 180°C (356°F), checking with the thermometer. The oil should shimmer without smoking.

doneness_cues.visual: The oil shimmers and remains free of smoke.

instructions.text: Fry the egg mixture by pouring it steadily into the center of the hot oil from just above the pan. Cook for about 2 minutes, then turn with the wide slotted spatula and cook for another 1–2 minutes. Adjust the heat to prevent burning. The thickest center, including the pork, must reach at least 71°C (160°F), checked with the cleaned thermometer inserted sideways; continue cooking if needed.

doneness_cues.visual: Both sides are golden, the edges are crisp, and no liquid egg remains.
doneness_cues.tactile: The center is set and lightly springy.

tips: Keep the omelet spread across the pan rather than folding it, so the minced pork cooks evenly.
Cook ground pork and egg dishes to at least 71°C (160°F), following [FoodSafety.gov minimum-temperature guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).

instructions.text: Drain the omelet on the slotted spatula over the pan for about 20 seconds, allowing excess oil to drip back into the frying bath.
Plate the hot jasmine rice and lay the omelet over it. Serve immediately while the edges are crisp and the center is airy.

troubleshooting.symptom: The omelet is flat and greasy.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The oil was too cool, or the egg mixture was insufficiently aerated.
troubleshooting.prevention: Beat until frothy and verify that the oil reaches 180°C (356°F) before adding the eggs.
troubleshooting.fix: Drain thoroughly and serve immediately. The original airy structure cannot be restored.

troubleshooting.symptom: The exterior browns before the center reaches 71°C (160°F).
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The heat is too high, or the pork remains in large clumps.
troubleshooting.prevention: Disperse the pork finely and keep the omelet flat rather than folded.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the heat and continue frying, turning as needed, until the thickest center reaches at least 71°C (160°F).

chef_notes: Have the rice ready before frying; the omelet tastes best immediately after leaving the oil.
Small, evenly dispersed pieces of pork preserve the airy egg structure and cook more evenly than dense clumps.
Frothy eggs and hot oil work together to create the characteristic puffed center and lacy edges.
Avoid pressing the omelet flat with the spatula, which compresses its delicate interior.
data.cultural_context: Khai jiao moo sap is a familiar Thai comfort food and made-to-order street-food dish featuring minced pork cooked into beaten eggs. Frying in generous hot oil creates its distinctive golden exterior, and serving it over rice makes a complete meal.
